units: <cite ref="Shevuot 47a:5">Shebu. 47ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>חזרה השבועה למקומה</he>, <cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 7:4">ib. VII, 4</cite>) <he>חזרה … לס׳</he> the oath (which ought to have been administered to one of the contestants) goes back to Sinai, i.e. the case is referred to Divine Justice that proclaimed from Sinai, ‘thou shalt not rob’, on which all Israelites are sworn. Ib. 22ᵇ, a. fr. <he>מושבע ועומד מהר ס׳ הוא</he> does he not stand sworn (not to eat it) from Mount Sinai? <cite ref="Makkot 22a:11">Macc. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>לא קא חלה … מושבע ועומד מהר ס׳ הוא</he> the oath (not to plough on the Holy Day) takes no effect, because he stands sworn &c.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:1">Ab. I, 1</cite> <he>משה קבל תורה מס׳</he> Moses received the Law from Sinai (by revelation); a. v. fr.—<he>הלכה למשה מס׳</he>, v. <cite ref="E00566"><he>הֲלָכָה</he></cite>.—
Sot. 21ᵃ דרשיה … כי ס׳ R. M. interpreted that verse (Cant. VIII, 7) like a revelation; Arakh. 30ᵇ.—Trnsf. erudite scholar.

<cite ref="Horayot 14a:4">Hor. 14ᵃ</cite>, opp. to <he>עוקר הרים</he> (v. <cite ref="E00808"><he>הַר</he></cite>) dialectician; <cite ref="Berakhot 64a:3">Ber. 64ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Moed Katan 12a:15">M. Kat. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>ס׳ אמר הלכה וכ׳</he> Sinai (R. Joseph) has said &c. (and you dare to differ?).
